task.title: Memory cleanup returns complete, contract-valid JSON on LinkAPI Gemini connections
task.source: Direct user report and live Harlequin reproduction on the Raspberry Pi.
task.classification: memory cleanup prompt and provider compatibility

coreClaim: Memory cleanup gives structured-output providers enough completion budget and an explicit proposal schema so analysis does not fail on truncated or contract-invalid JSON.
rootCause: The cleanup request capped the entire Gemini completion at 1,200 tokens while the selected LinkAPI connection spent nearly all of that budget on reasoning. The surviving response ended mid-JSON. The prompt also named proposal types without specifying their exact field and reason contracts.

inScope: Memory cleanup structured proposal prompt contract
Focused regression coverage for the request and prompt
outOfScope: Memory persistence or cleanup apply behavior
Chat, roleplay, or game generation prompts

claimBoundary.coreClaim: The previously failing Harlequin cleanup group now returns complete JSON with the exact sourceIds, replacement, and reason fields accepted by the existing validator.
entrypoints: Character Memories -> Tidy memories -> Analyze memories
legacyPathsOrFormats: Providers that ignore responseFormat still receive the exact JSON proposal schema in prompt text.
Providers that do not support adjustable reasoning still receive the larger output budget.
Existing fenced JSON parsing and proposal validation remain unchanged.
positiveRowsTested: Live LinkAPI Gemini response for the exact previously truncated Harlequin candidate group
negativeRowsTested: Unrelated memories excluded from the model request
groundTruthFacts: The failing live response had finishReason=length, 1,148 thought tokens, and 48 candidate tokens under the 1,200-token cap.
The repaired live replay had finishReason=stop and parsed into the existing proposal contract.
claimBoundary.userActionCopy: No new user action or copy is introduced.
outOfScopeClaims: This change does not alter which memories are selected as cleanup candidates.
This change does not bypass validation or apply any proposal automatically.
This change does not claim every provider will honor no-reasoning parameters.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: A structured memory-cleanup request could exhaust its completion budget on hidden reasoning and did not tell the model the exact accepted proposal shape.
contractLaneGate.consumer: Configured LLM provider followed by normalizeModelProposal
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: The producer must request enough structured output and state the exact schema that the consumer validates.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: The request now uses JSON-object mode, cross-provider no-reasoning controls, a 4,096-token cap, and explicit field and reason shapes.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: Mode-neutral engine generation owns memory cleanup prompt semantics and request parameters.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not loosen JSON parsing, silently accept partial output, or add a UI retry around a broken generation contract.
regressionProof: src/engine/generation/memory-cleanup.spec.ts asserts the exact proposal field and reason instructions.
The exact live Harlequin group returned finishReason=stop with validator-compatible JSON.

positiveRows.claim: The focused memory cleanup behavior remains correct.
positiveRows.evidence: Three focused files passed with 28 tests, including fenced JSON parsing, proposal validation, candidate preparation, and cleanup adapters.

positiveRows.claim: The exact live failure now completes with usable JSON.
positiveRows.evidence: A sanitized replay of Harlequin model group 1 through the running Pi runtime returned finishReason=stop with sourceIds, replacement content/kind, and the exact Overlapping memories reason.

positiveRows.claim: The TypeScript and architecture boundaries remain valid.
positiveRows.evidence: pnpm typecheck and pnpm check:architecture passed in the isolated worktree.

contradictionRows.claim: The fix must not accept incomplete JSON as success.
contradictionRows.evidence: parseJsonObject and all existing validation remain unchanged; malformed or incomplete JSON still fails visibly.

contradictionRows.claim: The fix must not alter memory records during analysis.
contradictionRows.evidence: Only the analysis request and prompt changed; storage and apply paths are untouched.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Providers that already returned valid JSON continue through the same parser and validator.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: Existing valid JSON and fenced JSON regression tests still pass.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: Providers that ignore JSON mode still receive a complete textual schema.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT includes exact keep_one, combine, and conflict object shapes and exact reason strings.

untestedRows: The complete ten-group Harlequin cleanup run will be rechecked after the merged build is deployed to the Pi; no proposal will be applied.

ownedFacts.description: Memory cleanup analysis is owned by the TypeScript engine and uses the shared LLM gateway without changing provider transport.
ownedFacts.evidence: src/engine/generation/memory-cleanup.ts imports only engine contracts, entities, and the LlmGateway capability.

ownedFacts.description: The existing validator requires sourceIds, a replacement object for combine proposals, and enumerated reason strings.

verification.baselineEvidence: The composite gate passed through check:frontend before the Windows harness stopped displaying the chain. Every remaining stage then passed separately: docs, Pi container distribution, Bunny guidance, PR-aware discovery, agent workflow, launcher safety, main protection, Rust workspace check, and the warning-only unused-code report.

notes: No user memory content is recorded in this ledger.
The PR remains unmerged until local checks, hosted CI, current-head Bunny, and PR health are clean.
